correctness.rationale: For arbitrary d≥2 and q_i≥2 the intrinsic graph Čech nerve generated by unit closed balls equals the simplicial downward closure of graph balls B(c)=c+S (a common interior-edge intersection of centered balls yields a common graph-vertex intersection). For nontrivial subgroup H≤T, a fixed realization point has support a union of entire cosets x+H with orbit-constant barycentric weights; quotient simplices are exactly cosets jointly fitting in a ball. The critical affine-coset lemma is sound: an affine H-coset in union of coordinate axes either lies on one axis, forcing H≤T_i, or meets two axes with elements u=a e_i, v=b e_j; applying ±2(v−u) forces 2a=2b=0, and translation closure forbids a third point, so H={0,a e_i+b e_j}. Coordinate H gives separate full simplices of q_i/|H| cosets on each of |T|/q_i parallel lines, with residual T/H-equivariant retraction to T/T_i. The two-axis involution has exactly one two-point coset per ball, hence |T|/2 isolated orbit points, regular under T/H; all others empty. Integral H~0 is the augmentation kernel of the corresponding permutation module. Independent complete subgroup/coset/ball enumeration for shapes (2,2),(2,3),(3,3),(2,2,2),(2,4) matched every case; source verifies another 200 mixed/composite and 500 prime subgroup cases only as finite corroboration.
